beats.text: A rocket that only goes up falls straight back down.
To stay in orbit, you need sideways speed. About seven point seven kilometers a second.
Straight up just fights gravity and wastes fuel.
So it climbs through the thick air first, then tips over, little by little.
Gravity itself helps bend the path. It's called a gravity turn.
Near the top, the path is almost flat. Sideways, above the air.
A rocket doesn't go up to reach space. It goes sideways to stay there.
